fine_trace.code: static int handle_data_frame(h2o_http2_conn_t *conn, h2o_http2_frame_t *frame, const char **err_desc)
fine_trace.note: Attacker-controlled HTTP/2 DATA frame carrying the END_STREAM flag is received on stream 1 while the request body is being streamed to the reverse-proxy handler (/reproxy-test, has_body_stream=1).
Because the stream state is still H2O_HTTP2_STREAM_STATE_RECV_BODY, the END_STREAM DATA frame is dispatched to the request-body chunk callback (write_req_chunk) with is_end_stream=1.

In streaming body mode (_write_req_chunk_done != NULL) the END_STREAM branch clears the done flag and the chunk callback, but never advances the stream state out of RECV_BODY and never sends an error (RST_STREAM/STREAM_CLOSED). The stream is left in a state where data received after end_of_stream is not rejected.

A further DATA frame sent after end_of_stream arrives while stream->state is still H2O_HTTP2_STREAM_STATE_RECV_BODY, so the only guard that would send an error (H2O_HTTP2_ERROR_STREAM_CLOSED) is bypassed.

The post-end_of_stream DATA frame is dispatched to stream->req._write_req_chunk.cb which was cleared to NULL by the END_STREAM handling (NULL function-pointer call -> crash), or forwarded to the upstream when the proxy had already replaced the callback; in neither case does the server send an error for data received after end_of_stream.

vuln_logic.issue_alignment: In streaming body mode the server does not send an error when receiving data after end_of_stream: the END_STREAM branch of write_req_chunk clears the chunk callback without transitioning the HTTP/2 stream state or emitting RST_STREAM, so a subsequent DATA frame bypasses the STREAM_CLOSED guard in handle_data_frame and is dispatched to a NULL callback (crash) instead of being rejected with an error.
